purpose: Audit every named Osiris burial/tomb claim currently identified in the classical source layer, separate whole-body tomb claims from relic-locality claims, and convert intentional multiplicity of tombs into a provenance-search graph.

observation_marker.note: Retained only as a narrative timestamp/symmetry marker; it is not used to score evidence.

core_hypothesis.statement: Plutarch and Diodorus preserve traditions in which Isis intentionally multiplies burial claims/effigies so that Typhon/Seth cannot identify the true tomb. This can create an intentionally forked provenance graph even without any physical violation of causality.
core_hypothesis.claim_ceiling: Intentional information obfuscation in the literary tradition does not prove that any modern archaeological site contains a literal divine body part.

named_whole_body_or_tomb_claims.ancient_claim: Plutarch describes a sacred island by Philae with an Osiris tomb; Diodorus reports a tradition placing the bodies of Osiris and Isis on the sacred island near Philae.
named_whole_body_or_tomb_claims.modern_location: Bigeh Island / Abaton, near Philae, Aswan
named_whole_body_or_tomb_claims.archaeological_state: Osiris temple/Abaton is archaeologically identifiable; published conservation research notes the site is partially submerged and has been studied by XRD/XRF/Raman and microscopy.
named_whole_body_or_tomb_claims.next_action: Audit excavation, conservation and object-removal records from Bigeh/Abaton for sealed reliquary, shrine, cavity, deposit and body-part-labelled contexts.

named_whole_body_or_tomb_claims.ancient_claim: Plutarch says elite Egyptians sought burial at Abydos to share ground with Osiris; later Egyptian tradition treated the tomb of king Djer as one of the tombs of Osiris.
named_whole_body_or_tomb_claims.archaeological_state: Major excavated cult/funerary landscape with Djer tomb and later Osirian reinterpretation.
named_whole_body_or_tomb_claims.next_action: Separate Djer-tomb, Osireion, temple precinct and later ritual deposit inventories; search hidden/sealed/nested objects and conservation imaging.

named_whole_body_or_tomb_claims.ancient_claim: Eudoxus, quoted by Plutarch, says Osiris's body lies at Busiris; Busiris/Djedu was a major Osiris cult center.
named_whole_body_or_tomb_claims.modern_location: Abu Sir Bana / Djedu, Nile Delta
named_whole_body_or_tomb_claims.archaeological_state: Cult center historically identified, but the specific alleged divine tomb is not archaeologically verified.
named_whole_body_or_tomb_claims.next_action: Resolve excavation corpus and museum distributions from Djedu/Abu Sir Bana; prioritize Osiris/Djed/Andjety objects with sealed or internal volume.

named_whole_body_or_tomb_claims.ancient_claim: Plutarch says Osiris's body also lies in Memphis; Diodorus preserves Memphis as one side of an alternative burial tradition contrasted with Philae.
named_whole_body_or_tomb_claims.archaeological_state: Large archaeological zone; claim does not identify one specific tomb.
named_whole_body_or_tomb_claims.next_action: Narrow through Osiris-Apis-Sokar contexts and old excavation object groups before any imaging audit.

named_whole_body_or_tomb_claims.ancient_claim: Plutarch/Eudoxus associates Taphosiris with the tomb of Osiris by name/etymology.
named_whole_body_or_tomb_claims.modern_location: Taposiris Magna / Abusir, west of Alexandria
named_whole_body_or_tomb_claims.archaeological_state: Archaeological site known, but scholarship cautions that the 'tomb of Osiris' etymology may be Greek interpretation rather than proof of an actual Osiris burial.
named_whole_body_or_tomb_claims.next_action: Audit Osiris/Isis temple deposits and sealed contexts, while keeping the tomb claim tagged as etymological/traditional rather than factual.

named_whole_body_or_tomb_claims.ancient_claim: Plutarch reports that a small town called Diochites was said to contain the true tomb of Osiris.
named_whole_body_or_tomb_claims.archaeological_state: Ancient place identification remains uncertain/unknown in the sources checked.
named_whole_body_or_tomb_claims.next_action: Toponym-resolution pass before museum or archaeological search.

named_whole_body_or_tomb_claims.ancient_claim: Diodorus reports some historians placing the tombs of Isis and Osiris at Nysa in Arabia.
named_whole_body_or_tomb_claims.archaeological_state: No secure target site established in this pass.

distributed_false_tomb_system.source: Diodorus I.21 and Plutarch De Iside 18
distributed_false_tomb_system.description: Diodorus says Isis privately told separate priestly groups that each alone was entrusted with Osiris's burial; Plutarch preserves a variant in which effigies were distributed among cities so Typhon would be unable to identify the true tomb.
distributed_false_tomb_system.consequence: A later map containing contradictory Osiris burial/relic locations is expected under the source model and should not be flattened into one chronology.

why: Late Egyptian Osirian relic lists identify the Mendesian nome as a seat of the phallus and spine.

An IFAO scholarly synthesis cites Dendera and Brooklyn 47.218.84: the Mendesian Osiris is associated with the male member and spine, and Banebdjedet receives an offering of a vessel containing the sexual organ in Edfu ritual material.
Papyrus Jumilhac/Khoiak traditions preserve a ritual finding of the phallus, which conflicts with treating Plutarch's fish-consumption branch as the only endpoint.
Mendes/Tell el-Rub'a is archaeologically identified and has excavation reports, a royal necropolis/object catalogue, museum-distributed finds and ongoing archaeological work.
critical_phallus_specific_exception.search_consequence: Mendes outranks the generic Nile/fish branch for a phallus-specific catalogue pass. Search for Banebdjedet/Osiris relic vessels, containers, foundation/temple deposits, gold/gilded small objects, sealed cavities and excavation object groups.
critical_phallus_specific_exception.claim_ceiling: This does not mean a literal divine phallus has been archaeologically identified at Mendes.

source_conflict.interpretation: The river story must remain one source branch, not the canonical last-known-location for the relic hunt.

steps: Resolve every named whole-body tomb claim to a modern site or UNRESOLVED state
Build excavation/museum provenance indexes for each resolved site
Search sealed, hollow, nested, reliquary, shrine and hidden-chamber object classes
Keep whole-body tomb claims separate from body-part/relic localities
Run a dedicated MENDES_PHALLUS_RELIC_PASS in parallel
Expand the distributed local tomb network using Dendera relic lists and Papyrus Jumilhac religious geography
